overview: Wall Street fell sharply on Thursday even as Anthropic's record $81 billion stock offering jumped 17% in its debut; the Dow and Nasdaq each lost more than 2%, and the selling spread to Asia and Europe on Friday. Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin left their 90-minute Shenzhen summit with a pledge on nuclear risk but no Ukraine agreement, and Putin promised a response "far more painful" than Ukraine's strikes on the Crimean Bridge. In Washington, the Senate passed a permitting overhaul 62-33 and blocked a resolution to end hostilities with Iran, while the White House replaced its national cyber director after a wave of tech outages. In New York, Mayor Zohran Mamdani proposed pushing the deadline to close Rikers Island to the end of 2032 and signed a law phasing out carriage horses by June 2028.

markets.summary: U.S. stocks dropped on Thursday: the Dow fell about 1,100 points, or 2.2%, the tech-heavy Nasdaq lost 2.3%, and the S&P 500 fell again, extending what the Associated Press called Wall Street's longest losing streak since 2024. Anthropic, the maker of the Claude chatbot, raised a record $81 billion and its shares rose 17% on their first day, but the debut did not stop investors from selling other stocks tied to artificial intelligence amid doubts about how much AI companies are worth. The selling carried into Friday, with Asian markets on track for their worst week since 2020, European technology shares falling and U.S. stock futures (bets on where indexes will open) pointing lower; Bloomberg reported Anthropic's own shares gave back more than 6% in early trading. Reuters reported that Wall Street's "fear gauge", a measure of how big investors expect stock swings to be, touched a seven-month high. The average 30-year mortgage rate rose to 7.28%.

movers.why: The Nasdaq fell 2.3% on Thursday and is down about 9.6% in a month, as investors kept selling AI and chip stocks despite Anthropic's strong first day.
The Dow lost about 1,100 points, or 2.2%, as the sell-off that began in technology shares spread across the wider market.

The average 30-year mortgage rate rose 17 basis points (0.17 percentage point) in a week to 7.28%; today's coverage doesn't give a single cause, though Federal Reserve officials signaled this week that they expect to raise rates in December.
Bitcoin fell another 1.8% to about $62,000 and is down roughly 25% in a month, sliding alongside other risky assets; today's coverage doesn't name a specific trigger.

concept.explanation: The VIX, often called Wall Street's "fear gauge", is a number that shows how much investors expect the S&P 500 to swing over the next 30 days. It is calculated from the prices of options, which are contracts investors buy to protect themselves against big moves; when more people pay up for that protection, the VIX rises. It usually jumps when stocks fall fast and sinks when markets are calm. It doesn't change your bills directly, but a high reading means the stock funds in a retirement account are likely to move more from day to day, and long stretches of market fear can make companies slower to hire and invest.
